  operations.person: "cast: the world's person this character is, by name or id, when the world spells their name otherwise or two people share it. Left out, the one their name finds is kept."

  operations.entry: "bind: the lore entry's id, as the lore map shows it."
  operations.memory: "bind: their entity's id in Lumiverse's memory."
  operations.defines: "bind: which side of them the source defines (background, appearance, voice)."
  operations.seed: "base: who they are, in two lines."
  operations.soul: "base: what drives them, and what they will not do."
  operations.inner_voice: "base: how they think, and how they talk to themselves."
  operations.background: "base: where they come from."
  operations.text: "growth: how they have changed from their base. history: what happened to them, as their story tells it. relationship: how they feel about the person, in their voice. knowledge: one short statement of what they know."
  operations.cause: "growth: what caused the change."
  operations.beats: "history: the ids of the story's beats it comes from. Each is checked against the story record; one the record does not hold is answered with the nearest beats and not linked."
  operations.with: "relationship: the person it is toward, by name or id. A character or the world's person it names is followed through a rename."
  operations.trust: "relationship: from -100 to 100 by default (the scale is a setting), when useful. A value past it is kept and said to be past."
  operations.warmth: "relationship: the same scale, when useful."
  operations.respect: "relationship: the same scale, when useful."
  operations.fear: "relationship: the same scale, when useful."
  operations.whereabouts: "away: where a principal who is out of view is, in your words."
  operations.place: "away: the place of the world it is at, by name or id."
  operations.names: "away: the people, places or things of the world it names, by name or id."
  operations.intention: "away: what it means to do, in your words."
  operations.until: "away: the story time the intention is meant for (a time of day, a part of the day, a date, or a span like two hours)."
  operations.how: "knowledge: how they learned it."
  operations.secret: "knowledge: a secret the lore marks that they hold, by the id the lore map shows. It is theirs from now on, as when a perception names it; given in place of another, the other is theirs no longer, unless other knowledge of theirs still gives it. A new entry needs text, a secret, or both."
  operations.told_by: "knowledge of a secret: who told them, by name or id; left out, they found it out themselves. Named as themselves, it is kept as first hand and said."
  operations.learned: "knowledge of a secret: how they came by it: authored, witnessed, told, inferred or guessed. Left out: told when someone told them, else witnessed."
  operations.belief: "knowledge of a secret: what they take it to be: true, false or uncertain. Left out: true."
  operations.sure: "knowledge of a secret: how sure they are, from 0 to 1. Left out: the setting cast.secretConfidence."
  operations.about: "knowledge: the people, places, things, quests or quest stages of the world it is about, by name or id (a stage as quest:<id>/<stage>). Each is kept by its reference, so the record follows it through a rename; a name the world does not hold is kept as you wrote it and answered with the nearest."
  operations.files: "filed: the old mind files carried over from the earlier build that have been filed into the record, by name (core.md), and the notes the older minds pack kept of the character (minds). From then on their agent is no longer given them; they stay on the record."
  operations.accept: "growth: true to accept a change a character's reflection proposed, by its id; false to set it back to proposed."
  operations.drop: "bind: true to take the source away. away: true when the principal is back in view. growth, history, relationship, knowledge: true to strike it; say why. Struck knowledge of a secret takes the secret back from them, unless other knowledge of theirs still gives it. filed: true to mark the files not filed again, so their agent is given them once more."
  operations.why: "cast: why this casting. With drop: why it goes."
  operations.source: "Where it comes from (not for bind or base): its kind alone (prose, lore, author, gm, character, player, default or invented), or an object with the kind in from. lore, message and roll cite an entry, message or roll by id; an invention cites its gap_check and consent."
  operations.precision: "How exact what you write is: exact, approximate, vague or unknown."
  operations.standing: "How sure what you write is: established, proposed or assumed."
---
Writes a character's record, as many operations as you need in one call: their casting, the sources bound to them, their base, their growth, history, relationships and knowledge, and which of the files carried over from the earlier build (their old mind files and the older minds pack's notes) have been filed. Casting, growth, history, relationships, knowledge and filing belong to this turn: if the turn is swiped or deleted, they go with it, and so do the secrets their knowledge made theirs. The sources and the base stand outside turns, and every version of the base is kept. The answer gives each operation's number, its op, the character and the id it wrote under, with the secrets knowledge made theirs and those it let go, a bound source's title, and the sources a base is older than; given as a receipt, it leaves what each operation wrote and how that part of the record now stands to the file it names.
